yesterday_verification_summary: For yesterday's verification (Sept 11 target), all numerical models accurately verified the precipitation call at Day+0, with ICON and Best Match pinning onset timing exactly, though surface winds ran higher than predicted across all models. narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Dry until evening thunderstorms. Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with rain becoming more likely.

## Today's Forecast
Thunderstorms and rain are expected to develop across Kisumu this evening, with onset anticipated between 18:00 and 21:00 EAT and rain probability reaching 95%. Total rainfall overnight is expected to reach 5.9 mm (0.23 in). Temperatures will drop to an overnight low of 18.8°C / 66°F following a daytime peak high of 29.8°C / 86°F. Peak surface wind gusts will reach 36.7 km/h (20 kt). Air quality is estimated at moderate levels with a CAMS model US AQI of 82; ground monitoring sensors are currently stale, with the most recent reading being an AQI of 70 at Kisumu Airport recorded 3 hours ago (individual station readings earlier today ranged from 32 at Dunga Beach to 70 at Kisumu Airport).

## Extended Outlook
Over the next three days (Day 1 to Day 3), daytime high temperatures will hold near 29.5°C / 85°F to 32.1°C / 90°F with overnight lows around 18.3°C / 65°F to 18.6°C / 65°F. Rain probability remains high (75% at Day+3), with light to moderate showers and thunderstorms reoccurring in the afternoon and evening hours. Looking further out to Days 4 through 7, maximum temperatures will moderate toward 26.3°C / 79°F to 31.8°C / 89°F while precipitation probability stays elevated around 70%, reflecting an unsettled regional pattern.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability is high this evening across all numerical models, with peak CAPE building significantly. UKMO leads convective energy estimates at 3260 J/kg, followed by ECMWF at 1980 J/kg, Best Match at 1950 J/kg, ICON at 1550 J/kg, and GFS at 830 J/kg, peaking around 19:00 EAT. Sudden, strong convective gusts are possible with any thunderstorm, regardless of the baseline background wind forecast. Heavy downpours may also cause localized surface runoff and temporary poor visibility.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Evening and overnight thunderstorms will affect Winam Gulf, bringing squally conditions to open waters. Peak surface winds will reach 36.7 km/h (20 kt), though localized downdraft gusts within convective cells may be considerably stronger. Boaters should exercise caution, as high convective energy across the gulf can generate sudden wind shifts, rough surface chop, and reduced visibility during downpours.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1008 hPa) and highest toward the south (1017 hPa) — a 9 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the northeast is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the west — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Locally across Nyanza Basin, mean sea-level pressure averages 1013.9 hPa with a 24-hour trend of +0.6 hPa. Basin-wide pressure snapshot points range from 1013.9 hPa at Kisumu to 1016.0 hPa in the higher terrain to the south, supporting moist lake-breeze convergence across the gulf basin.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Model weighting for today relies heavily on Best Match and ECMWF, which demonstrate the highest historical Day+0 rain verification skill. At Day+3 and Day+7, ECMWF and UKMO are given higher weight due to GFS's established tendency to over-forecast daytime maximum temperatures and under-forecast surface winds. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecast for Kisumu calls for a maximum of 28.0°C and minimum of 20.0°C with moderate showers and thunderstorms expected over a few places, aligning closely with numerical guidance on rain occurrence. Note that the underlying model guidance is at least 9 hours old (last aligned at 06:00Z), which widens uncertainty on exact onset timing. Ground AQI sensors are currently stale (last reported 3 hours ago: Kisumu Airport AQI 70, Ochieng' Avenue AQI 54, Dunga Beach AQI 32), so current air quality relies primarily on CAMS model estimates.
